name: Bandhani
hook: Thousands of tiny knots, tied by hand, opened like a secret.
origin: Tie-and-dye practised across Rajasthan and Gujarat for centuries. In Jaipur you'll find it, and its striped cousin laheriya, all over Johari and Bapu Bazaar.
story: A maker pinches a tiny point of cloth and wraps it tight with thread, again and again, sometimes thousands of times.
The cloth goes into the dye; every knot keeps a little circle of the old colour safe.
Then the knots are pulled open, and a field of dots appears like stars on a dupatta.
timePerPiece: 2 days for a simple cotton dupatta to several weeks for a fine silk saree

process.title: Mark
process.text: The design is stamped onto the cloth with washable colour, often using a perforated sheet as a guide.

process.title: Tie
process.text: Each dot is pinched up and tightly bound with thread. Fine work can mean dots smaller than a grain of rice.

process.title: Dye
process.text: The tied cloth is dyed, lightest colour first. For more colours, more areas are tied and the cloth is dyed again.

process.title: Open
process.text: The cloth is dried and the knots are pulled open by hand. The little crinkles are left in on purpose.

checks.real: Dots are slightly irregular in size and spacing. Hands, not machines.
checks.copy: Every dot is a perfect, identical circle in a perfect grid.

checks.real: Dots are raised, with a small crinkle you can feel with your fingertips.
checks.copy: The surface is completely flat and smooth.

checks.real: Turn it over: the pattern shows clearly on the back too, because the dye went through.
checks.copy: The back is pale or blank. The pattern was printed on one side.

checks.real: Each dot often has a tiny coloured centre where the thread sat.
checks.copy: Dots are a solid flat colour with sharp printed edges.

checks.real: Stretch a dot gently and the cloth springs back into its little puckers.
checks.copy: Nothing to stretch. It feels like any printed fabric.

gifts.name: Laheriya cotton stole
gifts.why: Light, easy to pack, and it brightens a plain kurta or a black tee.

gifts.name: Georgette bandhani dupatta
gifts.why: The classic Jaipur gift. Mothers and aunties approve instantly.

gifts.name: Fine-dot silk saree
gifts.why: An heirloom. Ask the maker how many knots went in; the answer is a story in itself.

quiz.q: You flip a bandhani dupatta over. What should you see?
options: The dot pattern on the back too
quiz.explain: Dye goes right through tied cloth, so real bandhani shows the pattern on both sides.
The knots leave tiny puckers. A flat surface usually means it was printed.

quiz.q: All the dots are identical and in a perfect grid. Most likely?
quiz.explain: Hand-tied dots always vary a little. Machine-perfect usually means machine-made.

tip: Rub a dot between your fingers. If it crinkles, smile. If it's flat, walk on.

name: Hand-block print
hook: Carved wooden blocks, a steady hand, and a thousand gentle thumps.
origin: Printed for generations in Sanganer and Bagru, two towns just outside Jaipur. Sanganer is known for fine florals on light grounds; Bagru for earthy colours and dabu mud-resist.
story: A craftsman carves a pattern into a block of wood, often sheesham, chip by tiny chip.
A printer dips the block in colour and presses it onto cloth, thump, lift, move, thump, all down a long table.
Each colour needs its own block, so one flower can mean three or four careful passes.
timePerPiece: 1 day for a simple stole to about a week for a multi-colour bedsheet with dabu

process.title: Carve
process.text: The design is drawn and hand-carved into wooden blocks. One block per colour in the design.

process.title: Prepare
process.text: The cloth is washed and sometimes soaked so the dyes take evenly. It's pinned flat on a padded table.

process.title: Print
process.text: The printer stamps the block again and again, lining up each repeat by eye. Outline first, then fill colours.

process.title: Fix
process.text: The cloth is dried in the sun, then washed or steamed to fix the colour. Bagru's dabu prints add mud-resist layers before dyeing.

checks.real: Tiny misalignments or overlaps where one block meets the next.
checks.copy: Every join is perfect, with no seams at all.

checks.real: Colour is slightly uneven, a bit darker where the block pressed hardest.
checks.copy: Colour is flat and identical across the whole cloth.

checks.real: The pattern repeats at the size of a hand-held block, roughly 10 to 20 cm.
checks.copy: Very long repeats or huge unbroken designs, typical of screen or digital print.

checks.real: The print soaks into the fibres and shows faintly on the back.
checks.copy: Ink sits on top like a layer and the back is almost white.

checks.real: The seller can show you the wooden blocks used, or tell you where it was printed.
checks.copy: No blocks, no village, just 'Jaipuri print'.

gifts.name: Set of block-printed napkins
gifts.why: Flat, light, and a little bit of Sanganer on every dinner table.

gifts.name: Double bedsheet set
gifts.why: Everyone back home will use it. Pick a soft cotton and a two-colour print.

gifts.name: Indigo dabu saree from Bagru
gifts.why: Natural dye, mud-resist, made in a village you can visit. Hard to beat.

quiz.q: Where two block repeats meet, real hand-block print usually shows…
quiz.explain: Blocks are lined up by eye, so small misalignments are the signature of a hand.

options: A mud-resist paste used before dyeing
quiz.explain: Dabu is a paste of mud and other natural ingredients pressed on to keep dye out, giving a soft, crackled look.

quiz.q: Which is a warning sign for screen print sold as block print?
options: A repeat the size of your palm
Perfectly even colour with very long repeats
quiz.explain: Screens print huge, perfectly even repeats. Hand blocks are small and a bit uneven.

tip: Look for the seams between repeats. A wobble there is a fingerprint, not a flaw.

name: Blue pottery
hook: Not clay at all, and that's the whole secret.
origin: A glazed craft that came to Jaipur with Persian and Mughal influences and was encouraged by the city's rulers. Its body is made mostly from quartz powder, not clay.
story: Makers mix ground quartz, glass powder and a natural gum into a dough instead of using clay.
Every piece is shaped, dried and then painted by hand in cobalt blue, turquoise and white.
It's fired at a low heat, so it stays light and glassy, but also a little delicate.
timePerPiece: About a week for a small bowl, from mixing to firing, with lots of drying time

process.title: Mix
process.text: Quartz powder, glass powder, fuller's earth and natural gum are kneaded into a dough.

process.title: Shape
process.text: The dough is pressed into moulds or shaped by hand, then dried and smoothed with sandpaper.

process.title: Paint
process.text: Designs are painted freehand with brushes, in cobalt blue, turquoise and other mineral colours.

process.title: Glaze & fire
process.text: Pieces are dipped in glaze and fired in a kiln at a relatively low temperature.

checks.real: Surprisingly light for its size. The quartz body is not dense.
checks.copy: Heavy, thick clay body that feels solid.

checks.real: Brush strokes vary a little; flowers on the same plate are not identical.
checks.copy: Perfect repeated motifs, often a printed decal.

checks.real: Glossy glaze with tiny pinholes or small bubbles here and there.
checks.copy: Totally uniform, factory-smooth glaze.

checks.real: Turn it over: the base is whitish and gritty-looking where unglazed.
checks.copy: Reddish or brown clay shows on the base.

checks.real: Mostly blues, turquoise and white, sometimes with green or yellow.
checks.copy: Bright off-palette colours like neon pink or purple.

gifts.name: Set of four drawer knobs
gifts.why: Tiny, packable and they turn any plain cupboard into a little bit of Jaipur.

gifts.name: Hand-painted serving bowl
gifts.why: Pretty on a shelf, perfect for dry snacks. Ask them to bubble-wrap it twice.

gifts.name: Large painted vase or platter
gifts.why: A statement piece. Many workshops can ship it home for you, just ask.

quiz.q: Real Jaipur blue pottery is made mainly from…
quiz.explain: The body is quartz-based, which is why it feels light and glassy.

quiz.q: You pick up a vase and it's very heavy. That suggests…
quiz.explain: Quartz pieces are light. Heavy usually means ordinary clay, painted blue.

quiz.q: Two flowers on the same plate look slightly different. Good or bad?
quiz.explain: Freehand painting always varies a little. Identical motifs often mean a printed decal.

tip: Pick it up before you fall in love. Light = real. Then check the base.

name: Kundan-Meenakari
hook: Stones in front, painted enamel behind. Turn it over.
origin: A royal jewellery tradition that flourished in Jaipur. Kundan sets stones in refined gold foil; meenakari fills engraved metal with coloured enamel, often on the back of the same piece.
story: An engraver cuts tiny channels into the metal, and an enameller fills them with colour and fires it, one shade at a time.
A setter presses glass or gemstones into place with thin layers of pure gold foil, the kundan.
Often several families work on one piece, which is why a good set takes time and costs what it does.
timePerPiece: A few days for a simple pair of earrings to several weeks for a bridal set

process.title: Shape
process.text: A goldsmith makes the frame, or ghaat, in gold or silver.

process.title: Engrave & enamel
process.text: Patterns are engraved, filled with enamel colours and fired, usually from the hardest-firing colour down.

process.title: Set
process.text: Stones are set using layers of fine gold foil pressed in by hand.

process.title: Finish
process.text: The piece is polished, and pearls or beads are strung on for jhumkas and necklaces.

checks.real: Turn it over: real meenakari often has detailed, glossy enamel work on the back.
checks.copy: The back is plain plated metal or flat painted colour.

checks.real: Enamel looks glassy and slightly raised, set into engraved grooves.
checks.copy: Colour looks like paint and scratches off with a fingernail.

checks.real: Stones are held by a thin gold-foil border, pressed in by hand.
checks.copy: Stones are glued in, with visible glue or rough edges.

checks.real: The seller tells you the base metal (gold or silver) and gives a bill that says so.
checks.copy: Vague answers about the metal, or 'gold' with no bill.

checks.real: Small irregularities in the enamel and setting from hand work.
checks.copy: Perfectly identical cast pieces, many of the same design on the counter.

prices.item: Meenakari bangle on brass or copper

gifts.name: Meenakari trinket box
gifts.why: Colourful, tiny, and safe to pack. Ask them to show you the enamel inside the lid.

gifts.name: Meenakari bangle
gifts.why: Wearable, cheerful and easy to size. Bring a bangle from home to match.

gifts.name: Silver kundan-meena jhumkas
gifts.why: The proper Jaipur heirloom. Insist on a bill that names the metal.

quiz.q: Where should you look first to check meenakari?
quiz.explain: Fine meenakari often lives on the back. A plain back is a hint it's a copy.

options: Fine gold foil used to set stones
quiz.explain: Kundan is the refined gold foil pressed around stones to hold them.

quiz.q: Good practice when buying precious-metal jewellery?
options: Get a bill stating the metal
Buy only on the first visit
quiz.explain: A clear bill with the metal and weight protects you, and honest sellers are happy to give one.

tip: Always flip it. The back tells you more than the salesman will.

name: Mojari
hook: Hand-stitched leather slippers that start stiff and end up yours.
origin: Traditional leather footwear of Rajasthan and Punjab, often called jootis. Jaipur's bazaars have whole lanes of them, plain, embroidered and beaded.
story: A cobbler cuts the leather sole and upper by hand, with no left and right at first.
Embroiderers add thread, sequins or beadwork to the upper, often women working from home.
It's stitched together by hand, and slowly takes the shape of whoever wears it.
timePerPiece: About a day for a plain pair to 3 or 4 days for heavy embroidery

process.title: Cut
process.text: Sole and upper are cut from leather by hand, using simple templates.

process.title: Decorate
process.text: The upper is embroidered with thread, zari, mirrors or beads.

process.title: Stitch
process.text: Upper and sole are hand-stitched together with strong thread, often visible along the edge.

process.title: Finish
process.text: The pair is shaped on a wooden last, trimmed and cleaned.

checks.real: A leather sole with hand stitching visible along the edge.
checks.copy: A moulded rubber or plastic sole, glued on.

checks.real: Stiff at first. It softens and moulds to your foot over a week or two.
checks.copy: Squishy and soft straight off the shelf.

checks.real: Smells of leather; the inside is leather or cotton lining.
checks.copy: Smells of glue or plastic; synthetic shiny lining.

checks.real: Embroidery is slightly uneven, with knots visible on the inside of the upper.
checks.copy: Machine embroidery that is perfectly even, or printed patterns.

checks.real: Many traditional pairs are straight-cut, with no fixed left or right.
checks.copy: Heavily shaped soles with foam padding.

gifts.name: Kids' embroidered mojari
gifts.why: Ridiculously cute and fits in a jacket pocket. Bring the child's foot length.

gifts.name: Embroidered leather pair
gifts.why: Goes with jeans and with a lehenga. Try both feet and walk around the shop.

gifts.name: Zari wedding mojari
gifts.why: For a groom, a bride or a very fancy party. Order a day ahead for your size.

quiz.q: A real leather mojari feels… on day one.
quiz.explain: Leather soles are stiff at first and soften with wear. Instant squish often means foam and rubber.

quiz.q: What's a sign of a hand-made sole?
options: Visible hand stitching at the edge
quiz.explain: Hand-stitched leather soles show their stitches around the edge.

quiz.q: Your new mojari pinches a bit. Best move?
options: Wear it around for short walks so it moulds
Soak it in water for a day
quiz.explain: A little snug is normal. Short walks help the leather shape to your foot.

tip: Snug is fine, painful is not. Walk ten steps in the shop before you pay.
